A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TailoredBench and contain complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C. Their content can be reliably matched despite section renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original performance-estimation and model-ranking experiments on five benchmarks, plus ablations and source-model analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations, sensitivity studies, and uncertainty plots.

M1.justification: The G-set probe, adaptive native-source selection, anchored K-Medoids extension, and calibrated estimator are unchanged between v1 Section 2 and v2 Section 3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ARC Challenge, Hellaswag, GSM8K, Winogrande, and POPE. The additional model-family and source-target similarity scenarios in Appendix B are also retained.

E2.justification: Random Sampling, AnchorPoints, and gp-IRT remain the comparators in Tables 5-6. The source-target similarity comparison retains AnchorPoints and gp-IRT in Table 12.

E3.justification: The reported random source/target split procedure, sample and model counts, correctness representations, and Kendall's tau/MAE metrics are unchanged. Both retain the default 10-example G-set, 20-40 inference budgets, and larger Hellaswag budgets of 50, 100, and 150.

E4.justification: Both retain the distance and calibration ablations, fixed-medoid and source-selection comparisons, G-set size sensitivity, model-family analysis, and source-target similarity tests. Appendix B's additional sensitivity and variance analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report averaging over 100 randomized trials, one-sided Z-tests over 100 repeated experiments, and the same significance threshold. Appendix B.8 and Figures 5-9 retain the variance/error-bar reporting.

E6.justification: The matched result entries in Tables 1-13 and the plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains ARC Challenge tau of 0.756 and MAE of 0.028 at 30 inferences; both versions report the same 31.4% average MAE reduction.

T1.justification: The formal setup, assumptions, and Equations 1-10 are unchanged. Diagram index corrections do not revise the mathematical definitions or derivations, and no proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: addressing prediction inconsistency through tailored coresets and improving evaluation accuracy at small inference budgets. The five-benchmark, over-300-model scope and 31.4% headline claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning prediction consistency, source-model quantity, and model-family affinity are retained. Both versions state the same limitation: comprehensive source-model predictions are required, creating initial evaluation costs for new or private benchmarks.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page footnote stating code availability and supplying the TailoredBench repository link. v1 has no corresponding method-code access information; other technical disclosures and model lists remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The new main-text Related Works section reproduces part of v1's Appendix A discussion. The reference lists and substantive positioning relative to prior approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: Part of Appendix A moves into a new Section 2, renumbering the method, experiments, and conclusion sections. v2 also adds an acknowledgment and makes small table-reference wording edits; the remaining prose is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-2 receive limited graphic and notation edits, including dataset-size index corrections. Figure 4 and several appendix tables move with page reflow, while the plotted findings and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new code-access footnote improves reproducibility documentation, while bringing relevant related work into the main text and correcting figure indices modestly improves usability and clarity. The method, empirical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
